profile.headline: Educator | Neuroscientist | Performance Artist | danbeekim.org
profile.summary:
-- Committed to building fun, compassionate, and multi-cultural learning communities --

15+ years of experience using live performance and movement games to teach neuroanatomy, physiology, and systems biology across university, industry, and community settings. Specialized in translating complex concepts into accessible, engaging experiences for diverse learners. Extensive experience developing curricula, mentoring students, and delivering high-quality instruction in traditional and project-based environments. Demonstrated commitment to inclusive, curiosity-driven education.

positions.title: Course Co-director
positions.description:
Co-director of Modern Approaches to Behavioural Analysis, a course that "will introduce advanced techniques for measuring and analysing behaviour, as well as three fundamental principles as necessary to understanding biological behaviour: (1) morphology and environment; (2) action-perception closed loops and purpose; and (3) individuality and historical contingencies."

"This course will emphasize the philosophical and observational skills required to understand behaviour, while also providing training in motion capture technologies and computer vision methods that can assist in the collection and analysis of video recorded behaviour datasets.

Focusing on the tool DeepLabCut, students will analyse either their own original video dataset or datasets of general interest and have the opportunity to practice tracking, pose estimation, action segmentation, kinematic analysis and modeling of behaviour."

 - Organized course materials and timeline with co-director Alexander Mathis. 
 - Evaluated course applications from prospective participants, who ranged from university undergraduates to post-doctoral researchers.
 - Delivered lectures on nervous system anatomy and physiology
 - Mentored and advised course participants with their course projects
 - Organized and coordinated course Teaching Assistants

positions.title: Course Director
positions.description:
• Designed and delivered “Modern Approaches to Behavioural Analysis”, an annual one-week intensive training course for undergraduate, graduate, and post-doctoral researchers.

• Taught conceptual frameworks for studying biological behavior, fundamental concepts in nervous system anatomy, and experimental design principles for behavioral neuroscience.

• Organized online guest lecturers, local teaching assistants, and a course Discord server to provide further resources and 24/7 support to students joining the course from locations around the world.

positions.title: Research and Outreach Scientist
positions.description: Led research and outreach activities at NeuroGEARS. This included initiating and nurturing new collaborations, managing client relations, and updating the company website.

positions.title: Research Scientist
positions.description:
• Conducted research on neural activity in naturalistic settings; developed tools for behavioral and physiological measurement.

• Communicated scientific findings to interdisciplinary collaborators and public audiences.

positions.title: Co-Founder
positions.description:
• Developed and taught a two-week project-based curriculum in neurobiology, physiology, philosophy of science, and robotics for high-school and early-college students.

• Created hands-on modules covering organ systems, sensory physiology, motor control, and homeostasis.

• Managed teaching assistants and mentored students through independent group projects.

company.name: Bartlett School of Architecture, University College London

positions.title: Theory Tutor, Masters Thesis Advisor
positions.description:
Theory Tutor and Masters Thesis Advisor for the Design for Performance and Interaction Masters in Architecture course. Responsibilities included:
 - prepare and deliver 2-3 lectures as part of Contextual Theory course material, introducing fundamental concepts in neurobiology and connecting the anatomy and physiology of nervous systems to foundational concepts in architecture, performance, and interaction design
 - participate in reading and discussing core course materials
 - mentor and advise 3-4 students per semester on their Design Thesis Report. Provide feedback on their written thesis and connect them to further resources. 
 - read and grade/mark final written theses of a portion of students in the course (each year's cohort is equally divided amongst course tutors)

positions.title: Tutor
positions.description:
• Taught biological principles -- including human physiology, perception, and systems neuroscience -- to graduate students in the Design for Performance and Interaction MArch course.

• Supervised thesis research, provided structured feedback, and fostered scientific communication skills.

positions.title: PhD candidate, Researcher
positions.description:
- Accepted into the International Neuroscience Doctoral Programme 2011, deferred admission for one year to write and produce an original musical.
- first year coursework (Jan 2013-May 2013): Techniques for Experimental Neuroscience, Cellular Physiology, Synaptic Physiology, Synaptic Plasticity, Neural Development and Anatomy, Computational Neuroscience, Sensation and Perception, Movement and Action, Neuroethology, Cognition, Brain and Body Loops.
- joined Kampff Lab in Sept 2013
- successfully defended my thesis, titled "On the Aims and Methods of Field Neuroscience: Non-invasive techniques for studying nervous systems in natural settings" on 17 Dec 2020

Lab Rotations
 - Costa Lab (Neurobiology of Action), Aug 2012-Dec 2012
 - Lima Lab (Neuroethology), May 2013-July 2013
 - Kampff Lab (Intelligent Systems), July 2013-Sept 2013

Teaching 
 - co-organized a week-long intensive course on Embodied Cognition: https://sites.google.com/a/neuro.fchampalimaud.org/embodied-cognition/course-information/schedule
 - Teaching Assistant, INDP 2014 courses: Introduction to Hardware and Software, Introduction to Techniques in Neuroscience

positions.title: Artistic Director
positions.description: • Developed neuroscience primer connecting anatomy and physiology of nervous systems to social structures and culture, adapted for learners ranging from 8 year olds to university researchers.

positions.title: Doctoral Researcher
positions.description:
• Developed theoretical and methodological framework for field neuroscience, integrating behavior, physiology, and environmental context.

• Benchmarked eye-tracking as a non-invasive measure of nervous system activity in complex environments.

• Designed and published a non-invasive technique for simultaneously studying single-cell neural activity and whole organism behavior.

positions.title: Undergrad Researcher
positions.description:
How Expectations Can Change Perception
Higher-Level Cognition Lab [Talia Konkle, Steven Piantadosi, P.I. Rebecca Saxe]
 - studied the effect of prior expectations on the perception of incongruent stimuli
 - designed and coded experimental tasks in Matlab
 - analyzed data in R

Observing Causal Laws by Tracking Eye Movements
Early Childhood Cognition Lab [Elizabeth Bonawitz, P.I. Laura Schulz]
 - studied how young children learn to make predictions based on patterns
 - tracked eye movements using Tobii Eyetracker software
 - analyzed data using Matlab
 - studies were conducted at the Learning Lab at the Children's Museum of Boston

projects.title: Neuronautas
projects.description:
A 2-week project-based summer program hosted at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown that empowered young people to follow their curiosity, question what is familiar to them, and confront the unknown. Our original curriculum combined systems neurobiology, philosophy of science, and robotics. 

Secured funding from the Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian in 2018 to operate as an Academia Gulbenkian do Conhecimento.

projects.title: The First VIRS
projects.description: An original young adult sci-fi graphic novel that weaves my doctoral dissertation into a narrative accessible to non-academic audiences. I recruited, hired, and project managed 16 illustrators, and liased with editors, administrators, beta-readers, Kickstarter funders, and a printing company to author, illustrate, and self-publish this graphic novel.

Co-director of Modern Approaches to Behavioural Analysis, a course that "will introduce advanced techniques for measuring and analysing behaviour, as well as three fundamental principles as necessary to understanding biological behaviour: (1) morphology and environment; (2) action-perception closed loops and purpose; and (3) individuality and historical contingencies."

"This course will emphasize the philosophical and observational skills required to understand behaviour, while also providing training in motion capture technologies and computer vision methods that can assist in the collection and analysis of video recorded behaviour datasets.

Focusing on the tool DeepLabCut, students will analyse either their own original video dataset or datasets of general interest and have the opportunity to practice tracking, pose estimation, action segmentation, kinematic analysis and modeling of behaviour."

 - Organized course materials and timeline with co-director Alexander Mathis. 
 - Evaluated course applications from prospective participants, who ranged from university undergraduates to post-doctoral researchers.
 - Delivered lectures on nervous system anatomy and physiology
 - Mentored and advised course participants with their course projects
 - Organized and coordinated course Teaching Assistants
